title: Ivo and the Smile
premise: Folklorist Petra Reyes arrives in the dying village of Hollowmere to record a lullaby the locals will sing only once, discovering that each performance feeds something sleeping in the old well — and that the family who shelters her, the Vances, have been keeping count for generations. When every mirror in the house begins reflecting one second late, the delay becomes a doorway, and the thing below starts climbing through the reflections into the rooms where the children sleep. Petra must choose between completing her documentation — which the entity needs to finish its own count — and burning her recordings to buy the family time to flee before the well refills at the winter solstice. In the end she stays behind as the living archive, singing the song backward to hold the thing under, while the Vances escape carrying only her notebook and the memory of her voice.
about_author: Wendell Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote coastal villages before turning to fiction. They write horror about people who cannot stop recording the things that should be left unrecorded.

chapters.title: The Song Sung Once
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She arrives in Hollowmere on a rain-gray afternoon and persuades matriarch Edith Vance to sing the counting lullaby exactly once, tape rolling. The village goes silent around the house while it plays. Emotional beat: the thrill of capture shadowed by the villagers' fear, as if Petra has just taken something rather than recorded it.

chapters.title: House of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She settles into the Vance household: Edith, her son Marek, his wife Lottie, and the twins Ivo and Sela. She notices salt lines under doorframes and mirrors draped like the dead. Emotional beat: warmth of found-family hospitality undercut by the house's quiet, practiced defenses against something everyone refuses to name.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ten-year-old Ivo notices his reflection blinks after he does — first by a heartbeat, then by a full second. He tells no one, testing it nightly with a candle. Emotional beat: childhood dread curdling into loneliness, the first crack in the world's ordinary surface.

chapters.title: The Well's Old Mouth
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek walks Petra to the capped well on the hill and finally explains: the lullaby is a count, and when the count reaches its end, the well refills with whatever was drowned in it long ago. His generation is the last keeping tally. Emotional beat: weary duty, a man passing a burden he never agreed to carry.

chapters.title: What the Tape Remembers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Reviewing her recordings at night, Petra hears a second voice beneath Edith's song — counting along, slightly ahead. She documents it obsessively, telling herself knowledge is safety. Emotional beat: scholarly compulsion becoming complicity; her prayer of documentation starting to sound like an invitation.

chapters.title: Sela's Invisible Friend
chapters.summary: Lottie's POV. Little Sela describes a 'wet lady' who watches from the hallway mirror and knows all the verses. Lottie scrubs the mirror until her hands bleed but the smudge of small handprints returns inside the glass. Emotional beat: maternal terror meeting the family's code of silence, love demanding answers duty forbids.

chapters.title: Generations of Counting
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith shows Petra the ledger — two hundred years of tallies, names of singers, dates of songs sung once. Every few decades an entry simply stops mid-line. Emotional beat: grim inheritance, an old woman's tenderness for the ledger that has outlived everyone she loved.

chapters.title: The Mirror Room
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo and Sela dare each other into the boarded mirror room where their great-aunt died. Inside, every reflection moves a beat behind, and one shows the hallway a moment before they enter it. Emotional beat: sibling loyalty forged in shared fright; the past reaching forward through glass.

chapters.title: Villagers Who Won't Look
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the village pub, Petra asks about the well and the room empties. Only the innkeeper's daughter, Brigid, speaks: her grandmother stopped mid-count in 1961 and the whole street heard the well 'swallow.' Emotional beat: isolation of the outsider who now knows too much, and the first ally outside the house.

chapters.title: Playback
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Playing the lullaby aloud to study the second voice, Petra realizes the room's reflection keeps singing after the tape ends. She snaps the cassette case shut and finds a wet handprint on the player. Emotional beat: the scholar's instruments turned against her; guilt arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: The Count Advances
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Mirrors throughout the house now lag by three seconds. Edith checks the ledger and goes white: the count has jumped decades ahead, as if Petra's arrival accelerated it. Emotional beat: blame surfacing in the family, loyalty straining as Marek wonders what he invited across his threshold.

chapters.title: What Was Drowned
chapters.summary: Brigid's POV. Brigid digs into parish records: generations ago, the village drowned a woman who sang to other people's children — a folk healer blamed for a fever. The lullaby is her song, kept alive so she'd stay counted, not forgotten. Emotional beat: horrified compassion; the monster reframed as a wronged mother.

chapters.title: Reflections First
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The delay reverses — now the mirrors show things a second before they happen. Ivo sees himself drowning in dry air and tells Sela they have to warn the grown-ups. Emotional beat: courage of a child protecting his sister, the found-family bond becoming the story's spine.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith admits the truth she's hidden: the count isn't keeping the singer down — it's feeding her, and the family are wardens who chose captivity over truth because freeing her means facing what they did. Emotional beat: shame and relief entwined; loyalty to a lie finally breaking against the truth.

chapters.title: The Well Begins to Fill
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Water sounds rise through the floorboards though there's no plumbing below. Frost forms the shape of a woman on every window. Petra calculates: solstice, twelve days, the well refilling when the count completes. Emotional beat: dread converted to purpose — she will get this family out if it costs her life's work.

chapters.title: Burning the Archive
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra burns her tapes and field notes, sacrificing years of scholarship, and the mirrors shudder back toward honesty. But the second voice now lives in her head, counting, and she understands the entity has chosen her as its new ledger. Emotional beat: grief for the work, resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Twelve Days of Water
chapters.summary: Lottie's POV. The household prepares to flee: packing, salting thresholds, teaching the children not to look at any reflective surface. Each night the water rises one step higher in the stairwell. Emotional beat: domestic tenderness under siege — meals, lullabies (sung silently), small jokes — love practiced as defiance.

chapters.title: The Wet Lady at the Landing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the last night, the woman comes up through the landing mirror, patient and dripping, singing the final verses. Ivo stands between her and Sela's room and sings the song backward, the way Petra taught him, and she pauses. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into fierce protectiveness; a child holding the line adults couldn't.

chapters.title: Solstice
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. At midnight the well crests and the house floods with reflections — every surface showing the drowned woman's face. Petra realizes the count can be broken only by someone willingly taking the ledger into themselves. Emotional beat: climax of choice; duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: The Living Archive
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra sends the Vances out the salted back door, then walks to the well and takes the count into herself, singing the lullaby backward as the water closes over the reflections. Her last documented thought is the family's names. Emotional beat: sacrificial transcendence — the documentarian becomes the document.

chapters.title: Out Ahead of the Count
chapters.summary: Brigid's POV. Brigid drives the Vances through snow past the silent village, the twins asleep between Edith and Lottie, the well's sound fading mile by mile. Behind them, Hollowmere's lights go out one by one, gently, like eyes closing. Emotional beat: exhausted gratitude, survival shadowed by the cost, found family bound tighter than blood.

chapters.title: The Notebook They Carried
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. Years later, Ivo reads Petra's salvaged notebook to his own daughter, skipping the last page, which fills with new handwriting whenever it rains. He teaches her the song only as a story, never sung twice. Emotional beat: bittersweet continuity — memory as both inheritance and warning, love outlasting the thing it saved them from.
